counterfactual_missing_items: No decreased accumulation, showed increased levels in the lesions
Normal blood gas analysis without acidosis
decisive_items: High-intensity areas in bilateral lenticular nucleus with lentiform fork sign
response.rationale: R4 is directly anchored to the defining imaging pair: bilateral lenticular fork-sign hyperintensity with an MRS lactate peak, favoring a specific mitochondrial/Leigh-type striatopathy. R5 shares only the less specific lactate peak and motor symptoms and remains a broad category. PD is contradicted by the DaT finding, Wernicke by normal B1, and Wilson’s disease has no raw support.

rejected.why: No raw support spans; lentiform fork sign alone is nonspecific for Wilson’s disease.
Parkinsonian features are present, but the DaT scan shows no decreased accumulation, directly contradicting PD.
GI symptoms are present, but normal vitamin B1 and lack of Wernicke-specific imaging make this unlikely.
It adds only age-derived adult-onset without independent diagnostic raw support; R4 already carries the specific imaging evidence.
